description: AGSC-00-23: a tool originates only what its declared version specifies, and where the construct is a value of a closed operator list the fault is AGSC-E203 — the code that already names a value outside a closed operator list — not a minted one (AGSC-09-15). Derivation, case by case. (1) `compose --emit executable`: `executable` is the target name AGSC-00-25 reserves to 1.1 for an executable Harness and its optimisation step, and the emitter registry of AGSC-07-18 is closed at 1.x, so the value is refused with AGSC-E203. It is a finding and not a usage error: AGSC-09-08 reserves exit 2 for an unknown verb, an unknown flag, a missing argument or invalid configuration, and `--emit` is a known flag carrying a value the registry does not hold, so the exit code is 1. (2) `export --steer --target wombat`: the eleven target paths of AGSC-01-28 are equally closed and an unregistered name takes the same code and the same exit. (3) A registered target is the control: the registry accepts `compose --emit gabbe` and reports no AGSC-E203, which is what makes the two refusals above a statement about the registry rather than about the flag. Whether the emitter itself is implemented is the distribution's own conformance claim (AGSC-10-05): AGSC-07-18 makes no emitter mandatory at any Level, so a distribution that ships none answers AGSC-E001 for the capability and still passes this case.
reason: Withdrawn for 1.0.0 (2026-10-06). Its third case allowed AGSC-E001 — the code AGSC-09-07 registers for an unknown verb, exit 2 — as a distribution's answer to a registered `compose --emit` target whose rendering it does not ship, while AGSC-00-20 says such a target is refused with the registry's code. Superseded by cli-0016: the same three cases, the third answered by the rendering (exit 0) or by AGSC-E203 (exit 1), never AGSC-E001.
